questions: A strong uneven bottom return and a second echo: what would you check first?
Gravel or another firm bottom
Deep silt
Definitely carp
I do not know
A strong return suggests firmness, but gravel, stones and clay need a lead check.
The bottom line is weak and diffuse. What is a sensible hypothesis?
Hard rock
Soft sediment
A shoal of carp
I do not know
Soft sediment can give a weaker return. Check how far the lead sinks and the condition of the silt.
Vertical returns rise from bottom. What should you compare?
Weed height on repeat scans
Moon phase
The colour of fish icons alone
I do not know
Repeated bands growing from bottom may be plants; verify with material on the lead.
There is a gap between weed beds. Where might a rig go?
In a checked opening or by a clear edge
In the densest weed
On any screen line
I do not know
Check opening size, GPS error and a safe route to land a fish.
After reaching a plateau the screen becomes flat. What else should you check?
Repeat the scan while moving and inspect the sides
Nothing: the top is always best
Only a fish icon
I do not know
The horizontal axis is time; a stopped sonar can make a section look flat.
You see a steep slope. Which position is the only correct one?
Only the top
Only the base
None: compare top, side and base
I do not know
Use fish activity, firmness, sediment and safety to decide.
A channel has soft bottom and a firmer side. What would you test?
Only its deepest bottom
The side and entrance, then perhaps the bottom
Always the middle of the lake
I do not know
The firm side may offer a cleaner presentation; assess oxygen in the channel too.
A partial arch and several dots appear in mid-water. What do we know?
Definitely carp
They may be fish, but species is uncertain
Always weed
I do not know
Shape depends on movement and beam geometry. Compare Raw and repeat passes.
A horizontal band appears in deep water in summer. What does it mean?
Certainly an oxygen boundary
Possibly a layer, suspended matter or noise: verify
Only a carp shoal
I do not know
Sonar measures neither temperature nor oxygen directly; another measurement is needed.
Bottom changes colour along one track. What next?
Repeat at identical settings and check with a lead
Change palette and sensitivity together
Certainly gravel
I do not know
Echo comparisons need the same palette, sensitivity and beam.
The header reads 23.0 ft. What is that in metres?
About 7.01 m
About 75 m
1 ft = 0.3048 m. Read the unit before comparing images.
Narrow has 1 cm target separation. Is a waypoint accurate to 1 cm?
Yes, they mean the same thing
Yes, if the bottom is yellow
No: beam geometry and GPS are separate constraints
At 10 m, the nominal 7° footprint is about 1.22 m wide. Target separation is not GPS accuracy.
A thicker bottom line changes from yellow to red in Day. What do we know?
The bottom is definitely harder
It may be a thicker soft layer; compare unchanged settings and check with a lead
It is definitely a carp shoal
Interpret thickness with reflection strength and palette. One line does not identify the bottom material.
